entities.how_described: 本集把它说成:Tom 自创的思维模型,用来对抗产品开发中的两种失败模式(盲目迭代与闭门造车写长线战略)。它要求团队在宏观大局推演(拉开风箱)与压缩成可执行的最小方案去交付(推回风箱)之间,基于新学到的经验不断反复拉扯伸缩。

evidence.quote: The phrase was play the accordion.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

evidence.quote: So the point of the analogy of play the accordion is if you think about a piano accordion, before you can play a note, you've got to stretch it all the way out, bring the air in.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_0

evidence.quote: What's a context where you have said to someone, "Hey, go play the accordion," or, "We're playing the accordion."
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

entities.name: 产品剧场 (product theater)
entities.how_described: 本集把它说成:一种只做表面功夫的反模式。指大量拥有 PM 头衔的人不去做真正的核心产品手艺活,而是沉迷于写讲故事文档、搞对齐会议、向领导传达战略框架等表演性行为。

evidence.quote: Marty Cagan calls this product theater.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

evidence.quote: We rewarded it for so long that it doesn't surprise me that that product theater is a core skillset for a lot of folks.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_0

entities.name: 系统思维 (systems thinking)
entities.how_described: 本集把它说成:面试 PM 时极其看重的、能展现出大局观的宏观思考能力。Tom 的训练法是「先想透最坏情况再干」:如果在产品评审时团队答不出「实验涨了会怎样、跌了策略又会怎样」,说明根本没想透,必须马上停下重新推演。

evidence.quote: And she said exactly what you said initially, which was the systems thinking, thinking big picture, thinking about the bigger business, and her advice there to work on this, and I want to ask you if you have any other advice here.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

evidence.quote: Say someone hears this, you're like, oh wow, I got to work on my systems thinking skills.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

evidence.quote: Thoughts on just how somebody might develop the skill and get better at systems thinking?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

entities.name: 微管理 (micromanagement)
entities.how_described: 本集把它说成:在脱离一线真相情况下进行的强行指挥。Tom 澄清,如果管理者不深入第一线的工单与数据去核对基本事实,就贸然从高处指手画脚,这才是有害的「微管理」;而如果基于同一套真实数据去深入细节,初级员工反而会备受鼓舞。

evidence.quote: So a couple things you've learned here for building, and I think in consumer, this is especially important, is counterintuitively to how maybe people think things should work, you're finding that the best teams, companies, products end up coming from top-down, founder-led, almost micromanagement is a dirty word to a lot of people, but it's basically being in the weeds is, in spite of how people may feel, this actually ends up being leading to better stuff, better [inaudible 00:55:56].
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_1

evidence.quote: And that's where I think the term micromanagement comes from.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_0
